title: Microsoft Teams: AI Interpreter for town halls and webinars
summary: Hold for licensing corrections: the captions comparison omits Microsoft's town hall exception, and the cost rationale incorrectly presents Copilot licences and Copilot Credits as alternatives. The roadmap facts and listed control paths and commands are supported; events-specific interpretation details remain unpublished.

claims.where: controls[0]; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No events-specific UI setting or automation for AI interpretation is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events AI audio interpreter languages voice simulation data processing default policy PowerShell. Opened set-up-events, interpreter-agent-teams and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; read its full syntax and parameters. No interpretation parameter or events-specific UI control appears.

claims.claim: No Teams admin center UI setting for managing Interpreter in meetings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Interpreter AIInterpreter Teams admin center UI meeting policy turn off. Opened interpreter-agent-teams and searched Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; Interpreter guidance says administrators must use PowerShell and search results supplied no admin UI switch.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AIInterpreter Disabled turns off Interpreter through the selected meeting policy.
claims.quote: To turn off Interpreter for your entire organization, use the following script: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AIInterpreter Disabled

claims.claim: The meeting policy AIInterpreter parameter is enabled by default.
claims.quote: The org-wide -AIInterpreter parameter controls whether your users can use simultaneous or consecutive interpretation during meetings in your organization. This parameter is enabled by default.

claims.claim: The meeting policy can govern particular users.
claims.quote: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies that can be assigned to particular users to control Teams features related to meetings.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The town hall control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy creating events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled
claims.fix: Add to controls[2].note: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference labels this policy as currently still in preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy.

claims.claim: The town hall policy controls event creation for assigned organisers, rather than interpretation alone.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The webinar control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Disabled prevents organisers with the policy creating events with up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Disabled
claims.fix: Add to controls[3].note: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference labels this policy as currently still in preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy.

claims.claim: The webinar policy controls event creation for assigned organisers, rather than interpretation alone.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars.

claims.claim: Changing the relevant event creation setting to Off after an event is scheduled prevents the organiser running or starting it.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: AIInterpreter in the meeting policy is not documented to govern interpretation in events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events AI audio interpreter languages voice simulation data processing default policy PowerShell. Opened interpreter-agent-teams and searched Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. Read plan-events excerpts: general meeting policies cover core capabilities, but Interpreter explicitly excludes events.

claims.claim: The Interpreter page says to use PowerShell to manage Interpreter for the entire organisation.
claims.quote: You must use PowerShell to manage Interpreter for your entire organization.

claims.claim: Teams town halls and webinars can include external attendees.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.claim: Interpreter performs real-time speech-to-speech translation in meetings using Azure Cognitive Services.
claims.quote: Interpreter performs real-time speech-to-speech (STS) translation using Azure Cognitive Services, supporting multi-speaker, mixed-language conversations in Teams meetings.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Interpreter agent page says simultaneous interpretation is available as part of the Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Interpreter agent is available as part of the Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Consecutive interpretation in meetings is usage-based and consumes Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Consecutive interpretation is charged to the eligible meeting organiser's applicable billing policy.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Related events feature
claims.claim: The meeting or event organiser must have Teams Premium for attendees to use live translated captions.
claims.quote: For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, organizers can preselect up to ten languages for attendees to use during the event without Teams Premium.
claims.fix: Add the qualification to the existing sentence: 'For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, organisers can preselect up to ten languages for attendees to use during the event without Teams Premium.' Keep the existing captions page citation.

claims.claim: A meter, rate or included hours for AI interpretation in events have not been published.

Read interpreter-agent-teams and Copilot Credits billing overview search excerpts; events pricing is not stated.

claims.claim: Specific role or licence prerequisites for configuring AI Interpreter in events have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams AI Interpreter for Events 576711 license prerequisites role billing credits rate. Opened interpreter-agent-teams and set-up-events; read event planning and comparison search excerpts. Roadmap names organisers but supplies no additional feature prerequisites.

claims.claim: The supported interpretation languages for events are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events AI audio interpreter languages voice simulation data processing default policy PowerShell. Opened interpreter-agent-teams; roadmap says supported languages without naming them. No events interpretation language list was returned.

claims.claim: Interpreter in meetings supports Chinese (Mandarin), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.
claims.quote: Interpreter supports the following languages for speaking and listening: Chinese (Mandarin), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish.

claims.claim: An AI-interpreted town hall has no human interpreter to correct a mistranslated announcement live.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams town hall webinar AI interpretation human interpreter correct translation live. Opened interpreter-agent-teams; read event planning search excerpts. Neither roadmap nor Microsoft documentation states that a human interpreter cannot also be present to correct an announcement.
claims.fix: Remove ', with no human interpreter to correct it live' from the hypothetical mistranslation sentence.

claims.claim: The meetings Interpreter needs a Microsoft Copilot licence or Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The experience is activated by a meeting organizer, who requires Microsoft Copilot (Premium) as a prerequisite, with Copilot Credits usage-based billing enabled through the applicable spending policy.
claims.fix: Replace 'The meetings Interpreter needs a Microsoft Copilot licence or Copilot Credits, so budget once Microsoft publishes the events model.' with 'Consecutive interpretation in meetings requires Microsoft Copilot (Premium) for the organiser and Copilot Credits usage-based billing; budget once Microsoft publishes the events model.'
